title: Generative machine learning guides experimental synthesis of LiZn₂Pt and NiPt₂Ga Heusler phases
summary: Researchers combined a generative probabilistic crystal-graph model (PGCGM) with an ALIGNN stability predictor to propose and screen ternary structures, then used the model outputs to guide synthesis. They experimentally synthesized phase-pure LiZn₂Pt and NiPt₂Ga; the measured NiPt₂Ga adopts a tetragonal Heusler structure rather than the model’s cubic proposal, with DFT comparisons supporting its lower energy. They also synthesized LiZn₂Pd as a human-selected follow-up that was not among PGCGM’s candidate outputs. This is one paper-level AI-enabled synthesis workflow and three related compounds, not three separate records.
ai_technology: PGCGM generative Wasserstein GAN for ternary crystal structures; ALIGNN graph neural network for decomposition-enthalpy stability screening
organization: Johns Hopkins University; Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory; Gdansk University of Technology

evidence.tested: Researchers combined a generative probabilistic crystal-graph model (PGCGM) with an ALIGNN stability predictor to propose and screen ternary structures, then used the model outputs to guide synthesis.
evidence.unknown: The reported synthesis outcome is experimentally characterized in the paper, but the AI was a candidate-generation and stability-screening aid rather than an autonomous discoverer: expert chemistry selected candidates and performed synthesis. LiZn₂Pt’s composition and Fm3̄m structure were already represented in Materials Project/OQMD training data, so its novelty is experimental realization rather than structure invention. The NiPt₂Ga experimental structure is tetragonal P4/mmm, differing from the cubic PGCGM proposal; the paper gives a DFT energy comparison. No superconductivity was observed, and magnetic ordering temperature for NiPt₂Ga was unresolved.
evidence.ai_role: PGCGM generated candidate crystal structures and ALIGNN screened their predicted stability. Researchers used these model outputs to down-select and choose Heusler-family candidates for synthesis. The authors note that expert judgment remained necessary and that LiZn₂Pt’s composition/structure appeared in the model training databases; NiPt₂Ga’s experimentally realized tetragonal structure was not the exact cubic structure proposed by PGCGM.
